# SPD-010 — Per-ticket Team card and Fleet.base#Team view

## Brief
Eric's stated need, 2026-09-12: click a ticket and see the lead, every spudagent under it with persona, model and status, and a summary of what they worked on and built. The spike's question 8 answer ([[SPD-006]]) proposes two pieces. (1) A `Team` view in `Fleet.base` filtered `ticket == this`, embedded in every ticket note as `![[Fleet.base#Team]]`; this needs no database and can land first on today's frontmatter. (2) A generated `## Team` table written by `spud render` from `members`: lead first, lineage order, persona (with `agent_type` for contractors), model tier and resolved model, status, run and duration, tokens and tool uses, and a "worked on / built" paragraph from `members.summary` with fallbacks to the first paragraph of `result` and then to `return_text`.

Part 2 depends on [[SPD-007]].

Done when: opening any ticket note in Obsidian shows the team table and the embedded view, and the summary column reads as a sentence about the work, not a status line.

## Size, persona and model decision
Two sequential children of Spud, both on opus, the persona tier. No Fable today (Eric's budget, 2026-09-12): any child or headless probe names a non-fable model, haiku for probes.

1. A designer, in the main checkout, because its deliverable is a doc and docs live on `main`: `docs/design/2026-09-12-team-card.md`. It settles the `## Team` table (columns, depth, tokens shown honestly, empty values), the "worked on / built" summary rules with a testable status-line rule, whether the tree list stays, the exact `Fleet.base` Team view with its `this` filter cited from Obsidian's Bases documentation, any new member frontmatter keys, the template text and the edge cases to test, with mock cards built from real ledger rows that Eric can open in Obsidian. Spud commits the spec on `main` and puts any departure from this brief to Eric before the engineer starts.
2. An engineer, in worktree `spd-010-team-card` (branch `worktree-spd-010-team-card`), implementing the renderer part in `bin/spud` with red-first tests.

The worktree is entered when the designer returns rather than at start, since the designer writes no code. Spudagents write nothing under `ledger/`, so the `Fleet.base` Team view and the ticket and member templates are Spud's own edits, made on `main` at merge from the spec, together with any CLAUDE.md prose; the embed shows once the branch is merged and rendered.
